resource.name: aws_elasticsearch_domain
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_elasticsearch_domain` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of Amazon Elasticsearch Service domains, providing scalable search, analytics, and logging capabilities for structured and unstructured data. Common use cases include setting up Elasticsearch clusters for log aggregation, full-text search, and real-time data analysis, as well as integrating with AWS services like CloudWatch for monitoring and Kinesis for data ingestion. Users can configure key features such as access policies, VPC integration, encryption at rest, node types, automated snapshots, and advanced logging settings to optimize performance, security, and reliability.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates the basic setup of an AWS Elasticsearch domain using the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource, including specifying the domain name, Elasticsearch version (`7.10`), cluster configuration with an `r4.large.elasticsearch` instance type, and applying tags. This example is ideal for users looking to create a simple Elasticsearch domain with minimal configuration."

examples.title: Access Policy
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an access policy for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource, using the `access_policies` argument to define fine-grained permissions with an IP-based condition. This example shows how to restrict Elasticsearch access to specific IP addresses while granting full permissions (`es:*`) to all principals."

examples.title: Log Publishing to CloudWatch Logs
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure log publishing for an Amazon Elasticsearch Service (AWS OpenSearch Service) domain by linking it to a CloudWatch Log Group using the `log_publishing_options` block. It includes the creation of a CloudWatch Log Group, an IAM policy allowing Elasticsearch to publish logs, and a resource policy to enable log stream creation, showcasing how to set up `INDEX_SLOW_LOGS` for monitoring query performance.

examples.title: VPC based ES
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Elasticsearch domain within a VPC, including VPC-specific options such as subnet IDs and security groups, while enabling zone awareness and advanced options. This example also showcases IAM service-linked role dependencies, custom access policies, and tagging for resource organization."

arguments.name: access_policies
arguments.description: (Optional) IAM policy document specifying the access policies for the domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `access_policies` argument for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to define an IAM policy document that specifies access control rules for the Elasticsearch domain, including permissions for users, roles, or services. By configuring this argument, users can enforce security and manage who can read, write, or administer the domain, aligning with common goals like securing data and enabling controlled access in cloud environments.

arguments.name: advanced_options
arguments.description: (Optional) Key-value string pairs to specify advanced configuration options. Note that the values for these configuration options must be strings (wrapped in quotes) or they may be wrong and cause a perpetual diff, causing Terraform to want to recreate your Elasticsearch domain on every apply.
arguments.llm_summary: The `advanced_options` argument for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to configure key-value pairs for advanced Elasticsearch domain settings, enabling fine-tuned control over specific behaviors such as enabling or disabling features like slow logs or custom endpoint settings. This argument is typically used to customize domain functionality beyond default configurations, supporting advanced use cases and operational requirements.

arguments.name: domain_name
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the domain. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `domain_name` argument specifies the unique name of the Amazon Elasticsearch Service (OpenSearch Service) domain, serving as its identifier within AWS. This required parameter allows users to define and manage the domain's namespace, enabling the creation, configuration, and access of the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch cluster for search and analytics workloads.

arguments.name: elasticsearch_version
arguments.description: (Optional) Version of Elasticsearch to deploy. Defaults to `1.5`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `elasticsearch_version` argument allows users to specify the version of Elasticsearch to deploy for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource, enabling control over the compatibility, features, and performance of the Elasticsearch cluster. By setting this argument, users can align the domain with specific application requirements or upgrade paths, ensuring the cluster operates with the desired version of Elasticsearch.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource represents the unique identifier of the Elasticsearch domain, typically used to reference the domain in other Terraform resources or outputs. While not required, setting this argument allows users to explicitly define or retrieve the domain's ID for integration, tracking, or dependency management within their infrastructure configuration.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument allows users to assign key-value metadata to the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource, enabling resource categorization, cost allocation, and environment identification. When used, it can override provider-level default tags, providing flexibility to tailor tagging for specific Elasticsearch domains.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the Elasticsearch domain and all associated resources. This facilitates resource organization, cost allocation, and environment identification, supporting common user goals like tagging for governance, billing, or operational management.

blocks.name: advanced_security_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for fine-grained access control. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required, Forces new resource) Whether advanced security is enabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `advanced_security_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to activate advanced security features for their Elasticsearch domain, such as fine-grained access control and encryption at rest. Setting this argument to `true` ensures enhanced security capabilities are configured, which is critical for protecting sensitive data and meeting compliance requirements.

arguments.name: internal_user_database_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional, Default: false) Whether the internal user database is enabled. If not set, defaults to `false` by the AWS API.
arguments.llm_summary: The `internal_user_database_enabled` argument in the `advanced_security_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether the internal user database is activated for managing Elasticsearch authentication. Enabling this feature provides a built-in mechanism for user management without relying on external identity providers, supporting use cases like simplified access control and security configuration directly within the domain.

blocks.name: master_user_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the main user. Detailed below.

arguments.name: master_user_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN for the main user. Only specify if `internal_user_database_enabled` is not set or set to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `master_user_arn` argument in the `master_user_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the ARN of the primary IAM user responsible for managing access to the Elasticsearch domain. This argument is typically used to define an external user for domain authentication when the internal user database is disabled, enabling fine-grained access control and secure administrative operations.

arguments.name: master_user_name
arguments.description: (Optional) Main user's username, which is stored in the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain's internal database. Only specify if `internal_user_database_enabled` is set to `true`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `master_user_name` argument allows users to define the username for the primary administrative user within the internal user database of an Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain. This configuration is only applicable when `internal_user_database_enabled` is set to `true` and is typically used to establish access control and manage permissions for the domain's internal authentication system.

arguments.name: master_user_password
arguments.description: (Optional) Main user's password, which is stored in the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain's internal database. Only specify if `internal_user_database_enabled` is set to `true`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `master_user_password` argument allows users to define the password for the master user in the internal user database of an Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain, enabling secure access control when `internal_user_database_enabled` is set to `true`. By configuring this argument, users can establish authentication credentials for managing the domain, aligning with common security and administrative goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The `master_user_options` block within the `advanced_security_options` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource configures authentication details for the primary user, including username and password settings. This block enables granular control over access management, ensuring secure administrative access to the Elasticsearch domain and supporting advanced security configurations.

"Enables fine-grained access control for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource, allowing users to configure advanced security settings such as user authentication and role-based access permissions. This block encapsulates settings for managing access policies and securing Elasticsearch domains, helping achieve enhanced data protection and compliance requirements."

blocks.name: auto_tune_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the Auto-Tune options of the domain. Detailed below.

arguments.name: desired_state
arguments.description: (Required) The Auto-Tune desired state for the domain. Valid values: `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `desired_state` argument in the `auto_tune_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify whether Auto-Tune functionality for the Elasticsearch domain is enabled or disabled. By setting this required string to either `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users control the automated optimization of domain performance and resource utilization, aligning with goals like improving efficiency or maintaining manual control over configurations.

arguments.name: rollback_on_disable
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to roll back to default Auto-Tune settings when disabling Auto-Tune. Valid values: `DEFAULT_ROLLBACK` or `NO_ROLLBACK`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `rollback_on_disable` argument in the `auto_tune_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether the domain reverts to default Auto-Tune settings when Auto-Tune is disabled. By specifying `DEFAULT_ROLLBACK` or `NO_ROLLBACK`, users can define the behavior for maintaining or discarding custom optimizations, aligning with operational goals like stability or configuration preservation.

blocks.name: maintenance_schedule
blocks.description: (Required if `rollback_on_disable` is set to `DEFAULT_ROLLBACK`) Configuration block for Auto-Tune maintenance windows. Can be specified multiple times for each maintenance window. Detailed below.

arguments.name: cron_expression_for_recurrence
arguments.description: (Required) A cron expression specifying the recurrence pattern for an Auto-Tune maintenance schedule.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the recurrence pattern for Auto-Tune maintenance schedules on the Elasticsearch domain using a cron expression, enabling users to automate and control the timing of maintenance tasks to optimize domain performance and minimize disruptions.

arguments.name: start_at
arguments.description: (Required) Date and time at which to start the Auto-Tune maintenance schedule in RFC3339 format.
arguments.llm_summary: The `start_at` argument for the `maintenance_schedule` in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies the exact date and time (in RFC3339 format) when the Auto-Tune maintenance process should begin. By defining this value, users can control the scheduling of performance optimization and system updates, ensuring maintenance aligns with operational windows and minimizes disruption to Elasticsearch workloads.

blocks.name: duration
blocks.description: (Required) Configuration block for the duration of the Auto-Tune maintenance window. Detailed below.

arguments.name: unit
arguments.description: (Required) The unit of time specifying the duration of an Auto-Tune maintenance window. Valid values: `HOURS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `unit` argument for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies the time unit (`HOURS`) used to define the duration of an Auto-Tune maintenance window. By setting this argument, users control the granularity of the maintenance window's length, ensuring precise scheduling for Elasticsearch domain optimizations and updates.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: (Required) An integer specifying the value of the duration of an Auto-Tune maintenance window.
arguments.llm_summary: The `value` argument specifies the duration, in integer format, for an Auto-Tune maintenance window in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource. By defining this value, users control the length of time allocated for automated performance tuning and maintenance tasks, ensuring optimal Elasticsearch domain operation during scheduled windows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `duration` configuration block within the `maintenance_schedule` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource defines the time span for the Auto-Tune maintenance window, enabling precise control over how long optimization and system tuning operations can occur. This block helps users ensure maintenance activities are performed within a defined timeframe, minimizing disruptions and aligning with operational requirements.

The `maintenance_schedule` configuration block within `auto_tune_options` for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource defines recurring maintenance windows for Auto-Tune optimizations, enabling precise scheduling of system tuning activities. This block allows users to manage the timing and frequency of maintenance tasks, ensuring minimal disruption to Elasticsearch operations while maintaining performance and reliability.

The `auto_tune_options` configuration block within the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables automated performance optimization for an Elasticsearch domain by managing settings related to Auto-Tune functionality. It encapsulates options for fine-tuning resource utilization and operational efficiency, allowing users to achieve enhanced scalability and reliability without manual intervention.

blocks.name: cluster_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the cluster of the domain. Detailed below.

arguments.name: dedicated_master_count
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of dedicated main nodes in the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of dedicated master nodes in the Elasticsearch cluster, enabling improved cluster stability and management by offloading master node responsibilities such as cluster state management and coordination. Configuring this argument is essential for high availability and fault tolerance in larger or production-grade deployments."

arguments.name: dedicated_master_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether dedicated main nodes are enabled for the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether dedicated master nodes are enabled in the Elasticsearch cluster configuration, allowing users to offload cluster management tasks like node coordination and stability to separate nodes. Enabling this feature typically improves cluster performance and reliability, especially for larger or more complex deployments.

arguments.name: dedicated_master_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Instance type of the dedicated main nodes in the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: The `dedicated_master_type` argument in the `cluster_config` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the instance type for dedicated master nodes, which are responsible for cluster management tasks such as maintaining stability and coordinating node operations. Configuring this argument helps optimize cluster performance and reliability by tailoring the master node's compute capacity to the workload and operational requirements.

arguments.name: instance_count
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of instances in the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of data nodes in the Elasticsearch cluster, allowing users to scale the cluster's capacity and performance to meet workload demands. Configuring this argument impacts resource allocation and supports goals like optimizing query throughput and storage capacity."

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Instance type of data nodes in the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `cluster_config` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the compute capacity and performance characteristics of the data nodes in the Elasticsearch cluster. By defining this argument, users can tailor the cluster's scalability and resource allocation to meet workload demands, such as optimizing query performance or handling large data volumes, aligning with typical goals like cost management and operational efficiency.

arguments.name: warm_count
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of warm nodes in the cluster. Valid values are between `2` and `150`. `warm_count` can be only and must be set when `warm_enabled` is set to `true`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `warm_count` argument in the `cluster_config` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies the number of warm nodes in the Elasticsearch cluster, enabling the configuration of a tiered storage architecture for infrequently accessed data. This argument is only applicable when `warm_enabled` is set to `true` and allows users to optimize cost and performance by defining the capacity of the warm storage tier, with valid values ranging from 2 to 150 nodes.

arguments.name: warm_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable warm storage.
arguments.llm_summary: The `warm_enabled` argument in the `cluster_config` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether warm storage is enabled for the Elasticsearch cluster. Enabling warm storage optimizes cost efficiency by offloading infrequently accessed data to lower-cost storage tiers, supporting use cases like long-term data retention or archival.

arguments.name: warm_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Instance type for the Elasticsearch cluster's warm nodes. Valid values are `ultrawarm1.medium.elasticsearch`, `ultrawarm1.large.elasticsearch` and `ultrawarm1.xlarge.elasticsearch`. `warm_type` can be only and must be set when `warm_enabled` is set to `true`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `warm_type` argument specifies the instance type for the warm nodes in an Elasticsearch cluster, which are used for cost-effective storage of infrequently accessed data. This argument enables users to optimize storage costs by defining the hardware configuration for warm nodes, and it must be set when `warm_enabled` is `true`.

arguments.name: zone_awareness_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether zone awareness is enabled, set to `true` for multi-az deployment. To enable awareness with three Availability Zones, the `availability_zone_count` within the `zone_awareness_config` must be set to `3`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `zone_awareness_enabled` argument in the `cluster_config` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify whether the Elasticsearch cluster should be deployed across multiple Availability Zones for increased fault tolerance and high availability. Enabling this feature (`true`) ensures the cluster is resilient to AZ failures, supporting multi-AZ deployments, and requires additional configuration such as setting the `availability_zone_count` in `zone_awareness_config`.

blocks.name: cold_storage_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block containing cold storage configuration. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Boolean to enable cold storage for an Elasticsearch domain. Defaults to `false`. Master and ultrawarm nodes must be enabled for cold storage.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in `cold_storage_options` for the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether cold storage is activated for the Elasticsearch domain. Enabling this feature facilitates cost-effective storage of infrequently accessed data, but requires both master and UltraWarm nodes to be configured.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cold_storage_options` block within the `cluster_config` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables the configuration of cold storage for Elasticsearch, allowing users to optimize costs by offloading infrequently accessed data to lower-cost storage tiers. This block encapsulates settings related to enabling and managing cold storage, helping users achieve efficient data lifecycle management and cost savings for large-scale Elasticsearch clusters.

blocks.name: zone_awareness_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block containing zone awareness settings. Detailed below.

arguments.name: availability_zone_count
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of Availability Zones for the domain to use with `zone_awareness_enabled`. Defaults to `2`. Valid values: `2` or `3`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `availability_zone_count` argument in the `zone_awareness_config` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies the number of Availability Zones (either 2 or 3) to distribute the domain's nodes across when `zone_awareness_enabled` is active. Configuring this ensures high availability and fault tolerance by spreading resources across multiple zones, aligning with user goals of improving resilience and minimizing downtime in distributed environments.

blocks.llm_summary: The `zone_awareness_config` block within the `cluster_config` of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables the configuration of zone awareness settings to improve fault tolerance and high availability for the Elasticsearch cluster. It encapsulates settings related to distributing nodes across multiple availability zones, ensuring resilience against single-zone failures and enhancing data durability in multi-AZ deployments. Configuring this block helps users achieve robust cluster architecture by mitigating risks associated with infrastructure outages.

The `cluster_config` block within the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource defines the configuration of the Elasticsearch cluster, including settings for instance types, instance counts, and dedicated master nodes. This block enables users to customize the scalability, performance, and fault tolerance of their Elasticsearch domain, providing detailed control over the cluster's infrastructure to meet specific workload requirements.

blocks.name: cognito_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for authenticating Kibana with Cognito. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional, Default: false) Whether Amazon Cognito authentication with Kibana is enabled or not.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `cognito_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether Amazon Cognito authentication is activated for Kibana access. Setting this argument to `true` enables secure user authentication and authorization via Amazon Cognito, aligning with common goals of enhancing access control and integrating identity management for Elasticsearch domains.

arguments.name: identity_pool_id
arguments.description: (Required) ID of the Cognito Identity Pool to use.
arguments.llm_summary: The `identity_pool_id` argument specifies the ID of the Cognito Identity Pool used to enable user authentication and access control for the Elasticsearch domain. By configuring this required parameter, users can integrate Amazon Cognito for secure identity management, allowing authenticated access to the domain based on user roles and permissions.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) ARN of the IAM role that has the AmazonESCognitoAccess policy attached.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role required to enable Amazon Cognito authentication for the Elasticsearch domain. By providing a role with the `AmazonESCognitoAccess` policy attached, users can configure secure user authentication and access control for their Elasticsearch domain via Cognito, aligning with common goals of managing identity and access in cloud environments.

arguments.name: user_pool_id
arguments.description: (Required) ID of the Cognito User Pool to use.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the ID of the Cognito User Pool used to enable Amazon Cognito authentication for the Elasticsearch domain, allowing users to control access to the domain via secure, managed user authentication. Setting this argument integrates the domain with Cognito for user sign-in and authorization, aligning with common goals of securing resources and managing access policies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cognito_options` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables authentication for Kibana using Amazon Cognito, facilitating secure user access and identity management. It encapsulates settings related to Cognito user pools, identity pools, and roles, allowing users to integrate Elasticsearch with a managed authentication system for streamlined access control and enhanced security.

blocks.name: domain_endpoint_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for domain endpoint HTTP(S) related options. Detailed below.

arguments.name: custom_endpoint
arguments.description: (Optional) Fully qualified domain for your custom endpoint.
arguments.llm_summary: The `custom_endpoint` argument in the `domain_endpoint_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify a fully qualified domain name for a custom endpoint, enabling them to define a user-friendly, branded, or application-specific URL for accessing their Elasticsearch domain. This configuration is typically used to enhance accessibility, simplify integration with external systems, or align with organizational naming conventions.

arguments.name: custom_endpoint_certificate_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ACM certificate ARN for your custom endpoint.
arguments.llm_summary: The `custom_endpoint_certificate_arn` argument allows users to specify the ARN of an ACM certificate to secure a custom endpoint for their Elasticsearch domain. By configuring this, users can enable HTTPS for a custom domain endpoint, ensuring encrypted communication and aligning with security and compliance requirements for custom domain access.

arguments.name: custom_endpoint_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable custom endpoint for the Elasticsearch domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `custom_endpoint_enabled` argument allows users to control whether a custom endpoint is enabled for the Elasticsearch domain, providing the ability to define a personalized URL for accessing the domain. Enabling this feature is typically used to align the domain's endpoint with organizational naming conventions or simplify integration with external systems.

arguments.name: enforce_https
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether or not to require HTTPS. Defaults to `true`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enforce_https` argument in the `domain_endpoint_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify whether HTTPS is required for all traffic to the Elasticsearch domain endpoint. Enabling this (default: `true`) ensures secure communication by enforcing encrypted connections, aligning with best practices for data protection and compliance.

arguments.name: tls_security_policy
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the TLS security policy that needs to be applied to the HTTPS endpoint. Valid values: `Policy-Min-TLS-1-0-2019-07`, `Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-2019-07`, and `Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-PFS-2023-10`. Terraform will only perform drift detection if a configuration value is provided.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tls_security_policy` argument allows users to specify the minimum TLS version and associated security policy for the HTTPS endpoint of the Elasticsearch domain, enhancing endpoint security by enforcing stricter encryption standards. By configuring this, users can align the domain's TLS settings with organizational compliance requirements or industry best practices, such as requiring TLS 1.2 or enabling Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS).

blocks.llm_summary: The `domain_endpoint_options` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables control over HTTP(S) settings for the Elasticsearch domain's endpoint, including options like enforcing HTTPS-only traffic and customizing TLS security policies. Configuring this block helps users enhance endpoint security and compliance by tailoring access protocols and encryption standards to meet specific requirements.

blocks.name: ebs_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for EBS related options, may be required based on chosen instance size. Detailed below.

arguments.name: ebs_enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Whether EBS volumes are attached to data nodes in the domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ebs_enabled` argument in the `ebs_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies whether Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes are attached to the data nodes in the Elasticsearch domain. Enabling this option allows users to configure persistent storage for their Elasticsearch data, supporting larger datasets and improving durability compared to ephemeral storage.

arguments.name: iops
arguments.description: (Optional) Baseline input/output (I/O) performance of EBS volumes attached to data nodes. Applicable only for the GP3 and Provisioned IOPS EBS volume types.
arguments.llm_summary: The `iops` argument in the `ebs_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to define the baseline input/output performance (measured in IOPS) for EBS volumes attached to Elasticsearch data nodes. This setting is applicable only for GP3 and Provisioned IOPS volume types and enables users to optimize storage performance for workloads requiring high throughput or low latency, aligning with specific application performance goals.

arguments.name: throughput
arguments.description: (Required if `volume_type` is set to `gp3`) Specifies the throughput (in MiB/s) of the EBS volumes attached to data nodes. Applicable only for the gp3 volume type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `throughput` argument in the `ebs_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the data transfer rate (in MiB/s) for EBS volumes attached to Elasticsearch data nodes when using the `gp3` volume type. Configuring this parameter helps optimize storage performance to meet workload requirements, particularly for high-throughput use cases.

arguments.name: volume_size
arguments.description: (Required if `ebs_enabled` is set to `true`.) Size of EBS volumes attached to data nodes (in GiB).
arguments.llm_summary: The `volume_size` argument specifies the storage capacity (in GiB) of EBS volumes attached to data nodes in an Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain when EBS is enabled. Configuring this value allows users to control the amount of disk space available for data storage, directly impacting the domain's ability to handle larger datasets and workloads.

arguments.name: volume_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of EBS volumes attached to data nodes.
arguments.llm_summary: The `volume_type` argument in the `ebs_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the type of EBS volumes (e.g., `gp2`, `io1`, `standard`) attached to the data nodes of the Elasticsearch domain. Configuring this argument impacts storage performance and cost, enabling users to optimize their Elasticsearch cluster for specific workloads, such as high IOPS or cost-effective general-purpose storage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `ebs_options` configuration block within the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables the management of Elastic Block Store (EBS) settings for the Elasticsearch domain, allowing users to configure storage options such as volume size, type, and IOPS. This block is essential for optimizing storage performance and capacity, particularly for larger instance sizes, ensuring the domain can handle data-intensive workloads effectively.

blocks.name: encrypt_at_rest
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for encrypt at rest options. Only available for certain instance types. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Whether to enable encryption at rest. If the `encrypt_at_rest` block is not provided then this defaults to `false`. Enabling encryption on new domains requires `elasticsearch_version` 5.1 or greater.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `encrypt_at_rest` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies whether encryption at rest is activated for the Elasticsearch domain. Setting this to `true` ensures that data stored on disk is encrypted, enhancing security and meeting compliance requirements, provided the Elasticsearch version is 5.1 or higher.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) KMS key ARN to encrypt the Elasticsearch domain with. If not specified then it defaults to using the `aws/es` service KMS key. Note that KMS will accept a KMS key ID but will return the key ARN. To prevent Terraform detecting unwanted changes, use the key ARN instead.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument allows users to specify a custom AWS KMS key ARN for encrypting data at rest in the Elasticsearch domain, overriding the default `aws/es` service KMS key. By defining this argument, users can enforce stricter control over encryption keys to meet compliance, security, or organizational requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `encrypt_at_rest` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables encryption of data stored on disk within the Elasticsearch domain, enhancing data security and compliance. It encapsulates settings related to enabling encryption and specifying the AWS Key Management Service (KMS) key used for encryption, allowing users to safeguard sensitive information and meet regulatory requirements for data protection.

blocks.name: log_publishing_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for publishing slow and application logs to CloudWatch Logs. This block can be declared multiple times, for each log_type, within the same resource. Detailed below.

arguments.name: cloudwatch_log_group_arn
arguments.description: (Required) ARN of the Cloudwatch log group to which log needs to be published.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_log_group_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudWatch log group where Elasticsearch domain logs, such as search, index, or error logs, will be published. This required setting enables centralized log management and monitoring by directing domain activity logs to a designated CloudWatch log group, supporting common user goals like troubleshooting, compliance, and performance analysis.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional, Default: true) Whether given log publishing option is enabled or not.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `log_publishing_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to control whether a specific log publishing configuration (e.g., for error logs, search slow logs, or index slow logs) is active. Setting this to `true` (default) enables the publishing of the specified log type to the configured destination, helping users monitor and troubleshoot Elasticsearch domain activity.

arguments.name: log_type
arguments.description: (Required) Type of Elasticsearch log. Valid values: `INDEX_SLOW_LOGS`, `SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS`, `ES_APPLICATION_LOGS`, `AUDIT_LOGS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_type` argument in the `log_publishing_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource specifies the category of Elasticsearch logs to publish, such as `INDEX_SLOW_LOGS`, `SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS`, `ES_APPLICATION_LOGS`, or `AUDIT_LOGS`. By defining this argument, users can control which type of operational or diagnostic log data is captured and sent to a designated destination, enabling enhanced monitoring, troubleshooting, and compliance for their Elasticsearch domain.

blocks.llm_summary: The `log_publishing_options` block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource configures the publishing of Elasticsearch slow logs and application logs to CloudWatch Logs, enabling centralized log management and monitoring. By specifying settings for each `log_type`, this block allows users to track performance issues and application behavior, facilitating enhanced observability and troubleshooting for their Elasticsearch domain.

blocks.name: node_to_node_encryption
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for node-to-node encryption options. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Whether to enable node-to-node encryption. If the `node_to_node_encryption` block is not provided then this defaults to `false`. Enabling node-to-node encryption of a new domain requires an `elasticsearch_version` of `6.0` or greater.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `node_to_node_encryption` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify whether node-to-node encryption is activated for the Elasticsearch domain. Enabling this feature ensures secure communication between nodes within the cluster, which is critical for protecting sensitive data in transit and meeting compliance requirements for Elasticsearch versions 6.0 or higher.

blocks.llm_summary: The `node_to_node_encryption` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables encryption for data transmitted between nodes within an Elasticsearch domain, enhancing security and protecting sensitive information during internal communication. This block encapsulates settings related to enabling or managing node-to-node encryption, helping users achieve secure cluster communication to meet compliance and data protection requirements.

blocks.name: snapshot_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for snapshot related options. Detailed below. DEPRECATED. For domains running Elasticsearch 5.3 and later, Amazon ES takes hourly automated snapshots, making this setting irrelevant. For domains running earlier versions of Elasticsearch, Amazon ES takes daily automated snapshots.

arguments.name: automated_snapshot_start_hour
arguments.description: (Required) Hour during which the service takes an automated daily snapshot of the indices in the domain.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the specific hour (0-23) at which automated daily snapshots of Elasticsearch indices are initiated, enabling users to schedule backups for data durability and recovery in alignment with operational or maintenance windows."

blocks.llm_summary: The `snapshot_options` block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource configures settings for automated snapshots of Elasticsearch domains, primarily relevant for versions earlier than Elasticsearch 5.3. It encapsulates snapshot scheduling options, enabling users to manage daily backups for data durability and recovery, though it is deprecated for newer versions where hourly snapshots are automatically handled by Amazon Elasticsearch Service.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform will wait for the creation of an Elasticsearch domain to complete. By configuring this timeout, users can control the provisioning behavior to accommodate longer setup times for complex domains, ensuring smoother resource deployment without premature failure.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "30m") Terraform will wait for the deletion of an Elasticsearch domain to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures users can control the lifecycle behavior during resource teardown, preventing operations from hanging indefinitely or timing out prematurely in cases where domain deletion is delayed due to AWS processing constraints.

arguments.name: update
arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform will wait for updates to the Elasticsearch domain to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures smoother management of long-running update operations, helping users avoid premature failures during domain modifications such as scaling, version upgrades, or configuration changes.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource defines customizable time limits for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting an Elasticsearch domain. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent timeouts in long-running tasks, ensuring smoother deployment and lifecycle management of Elasticsearch domains in AWS.

blocks.name: vpc_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for VPC related options. Adding or removing this configuration forces a new resource (documentation). Detailed below.

arguments.name: availability_zones
arguments.llm_summary: The `availability_zones` argument within the `vpc_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the set of Availability Zones in which the VPC endpoints for the Elasticsearch domain will be deployed. Configuring this argument helps optimize network routing and enhances fault tolerance by distributing resources across multiple zones, aligning with common goals like improving availability and reducing latency in a VPC-based deployment.

arguments.name: security_group_ids
arguments.description: (Optional) List of VPC Security Group IDs to be applied to the Elasticsearch domain endpoints. If omitted, the default Security Group for the VPC will be used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_group_ids` argument in the `vpc_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify a set of VPC Security Group IDs to control network-level access to the Elasticsearch domain endpoints. By defining this argument, users can enforce custom security rules, such as restricting inbound and outbound traffic, to align with their organization's access policies and enhance the domain's protection within the VPC.

arguments.name: subnet_ids
arguments.description: (Required) List of VPC Subnet IDs for the Elasticsearch domain endpoints to be created in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_ids` argument in the `vpc_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the VPC subnets where Elasticsearch domain endpoints will be deployed. By defining this set of subnet IDs, users can control the network placement of the domain within their VPC, ensuring private access, enhanced security, and compliance with specific networking requirements such as subnet isolation or routing configurations.

arguments.name: vpc_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_id` argument within the `vpc_options` block of the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource allows users to specify the ID of the VPC in which the Elasticsearch domain will be deployed. By setting this argument, users can ensure the domain is provisioned within a private network, enabling enhanced security and controlled access to the Elasticsearch service, which is a common goal for environments requiring restricted connectivity.

blocks.llm_summary: The `vpc_options` configuration block in the `aws_elasticsearch_domain` resource enables the setup of VPC-specific networking for the Elasticsearch domain, allowing users to define private access within their AWS Virtual Private Cloud. It encapsulates settings related to subnet and security group associations, ensuring secure and isolated communication for the domain, and requires resource recreation when added or removed, making it essential for achieving controlled and secure network configurations.
